macro.topic: Tera Portföy / TP2 money market fund crisis

views.view: Argued that DSTKF collateral inside the TP2 fund was about 25% of the fund (~50 billion TL), that since a single counterparty can be lent at most 10% of fund size Tera could have borrowed at most ~22 billion TL against that collateral, that the company's ~92-95 billion TL in equity could cover that debt, and that the problem stems from a liquidity squeeze rather than asset devaluation; sharply criticized the CMB (SPK) for not issuing a clear statement on PPFs.
views.quote: The DSTKF holdings inside TP2 were about 25% of the total fund. That's roughly 50 billion TL... Against that 50 billion TL of DSTKF shares, Tera may have borrowed at most around 22 billion TL from the TP2 fund... Tera's own equity as of June 30 also totals roughly 92-95 billion TL.

views.view: Relayed that Berk Dinçtürk, assessing the turmoil in the funds, said regulated markets are essential for global capital and flagged the risks carried by highly leveraged transactions.
views.quote: Assessing the turmoil in the funds and stating that regulated markets are essential for global capital, Berk Dinçtürk flagged the risks carried by highly leveraged transactions.

views.view: Criticized many of the country's 'respected' economists for not saying a word about the Tera fund crisis until now, and now churning out op-eds lecturing the public.
views.quote: Many of the country's "respected" economists haven't said a single word about the Tera fund matter until now, staying silent out of fear instead of warning people. Now they've come out writing paragraphs of op-eds, lecturing everyone.

macro.topic: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's wide-ranging interview

views.view: Relayed that from Huang's interview, AI reached a major turning point this year and token generation is now 'incredibly profitable'; that the US should use its most advanced AI chips domestically first, with Vera Rubin already in volume production and China years behind, though he strongly disagreed with Dario Amodei's call to stop selling powerful US AI technology to China; and that the industry admitted it didn't engage communities on data centers early enough.
views.quote: AI crossed a major turning point earlier this year: It became genuinely useful, demand surged, and token generation is now "incredibly profitable." The capability of the technology has now reached an extremely useful state.

macro.topic: Middle East/Ukraine geopolitical tension and impact on energy-oil markets

views.view: Said continued attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure and Trump's energy ceasefire failing to take firm shape are putting Europe back at serious energy risk before winter; that Yemen-Saudi Arabia tension and tanker attacks are raising a new bottleneck risk in oil supply; that if oil stays high, inflation pressure would rise, rate-cut expectations would fall, and risk appetite would drop; and that the Bank of Japan raising rates to 1.25% is also a separate factor for global liquidity; said he himself is holding his positions.
views.quote: If oil stays high, I think the chain is quite clear: energy costs up, inflation pressure up, rate-cut expectations down, higher-rate expectations up, risk appetite down... I'm holding my positions too.

views.view: Shared that after Ukraine launched a single-day attack of over 1,600 drones on Moscow, Nasdaq weekend futures fell about 0.35%.
views.quote: Ukraine launched a mass attack of more than 1,600 drones on Moscow in a single day. Oil facilities in Moscow are burning. Following the news, Nasdaq's weekend market fell about 0.35%.

views.view: Relayed that China's CXMT began mass production on its fifth-generation DRAM platform, reducing key memory-cell spacing to 11.95nm using quadruple patterning, and that it can produce at least 50% more chip dies per wafer than its prior generation, part of China's push to reduce dependence on foreign chipmaking technology.
views.quote: CXMT says the platform reduces key memory-cell spacing to 11.95nm using quadruple patterning, allowing more memory to be packed onto each chip... the new platform can produce at least 50% more gross chip dies per wafer than its fourth-generation process.

persons.name: dtfinans_
persons.digest: dtfinans_ calculated that the DSTKF collateral inside the TP2 fund was about 25% of the total fund (~50 billion TL), that because the reverse-repo limit to a single company is 10%, Tera could have borrowed at most ~22 billion TL against that collateral, that the company's ~92-95 billion TL equity could cover that debt, and argued the problem stems from a liquidity squeeze, not asset devaluation. Noting that Tera fulfilled all redemption requests in its TRJ, FSU, TMM and TRU funds, he said the odds of a problem in TP2 are very low. He sharply criticized the CMB (SPK) for not issuing a clear, separate statement on PPFs and flagged the desperation of affected investors.
